title: Corporate Strategy
completion_message: ¡Soberbio! El lenguaje de la Estrategia Corporativa es el idioma de los CEOs y las juntas directivas. Con términos como 'Blue ocean', 'Core competency' y 'Paradigm shift', puedes articular la visión a largo plazo de cualquier organización.

parts.visual:
Conceptos Estratégicos I: 
- Core competency (Competencia central / Habilidad principal que da ventaja a una empresa). 
Ej: Apple's core competency is design and user experience. 
- Competitive advantage (Ventaja competitiva / Lo que te hace mejor que la competencia). 
Ej: Their vast distribution network is their main competitive advantage. 
- Blue ocean strategy (Estrategia de océano azul / Crear un mercado nuevo sin competencia). 
Ej: Instead of fighting in a crowded market, they sought a blue ocean.
parts.audio: Strategic Concepts Part 1. 'Core competency' is a defining capability or advantage that distinguishes an enterprise from its competitors. For example: Apple's core competency is design and user experience. 'Competitive advantage' is a condition or circumstance that puts a company in a favorable or superior business position. For example: Their vast distribution network is their main competitive advantage. 'Blue ocean strategy' refers to creating a new, uncontested market space. For example: Instead of fighting in a crowded market, they sought a blue ocean.

parts.visual:
Conceptos Estratégicos II: 
- Economies of scale (Economías de escala / Reducción de costos al producir en grandes cantidades). 
Ej: Amazon achieves massive economies of scale. 
- Paradigm shift (Cambio de paradigma / Un cambio fundamental en la forma de pensar o hacer las cosas). 
Ej: The invention of the smartphone caused a paradigm shift in computing. 
- Bottleneck (Cuello de botella / Un punto de congestión que retrasa un proceso). 
Ej: The lack of microchips became a major bottleneck in production.
parts.audio: Strategic Concepts Part 2. 'Economies of scale' refers to the cost advantages that enterprises obtain due to their scale of operation. For example: Amazon achieves massive economies of scale. A 'Paradigm shift' is a fundamental change in approach or underlying assumptions. For example: The invention of the smartphone caused a paradigm shift in computing. A 'Bottleneck' is a point of congestion in a system that slows down the overall process. For example: The lack of microchips became a major bottleneck in production.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el término de estrategia corporativa correcto.

questions.question: The unique ability that gives a company an advantage over competitors is its core ____. (Competencia central).
Lower costs, better quality, and brand loyalty are examples of a competitive ____. (Ventaja).
Creating a completely new market space with no competitors is called a ____ ocean strategy.
questions.explanation: Blue ocean strategy = estrategia de océano azul (vs. océano rojo = muy competitivo).

questions.question: When the cost per unit decreases as the volume of production increases, a company achieves economies of ____. (Escala).
questions.explanation: Economies of scale = economías de escala.

questions.question: A fundamental change in the way an industry operates is called a ____ shift. (Paradigma).
A step in the production process that is too slow and delays everything else is a ____. (Cuello de botella).
A strategic planning technique used to identify Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, and Threats is a ____ analysis.
questions.explanation: SWOT analysis = análisis FODA o DAFO.

questions.question: The proportion of total sales in a market that is controlled by a specific company is its market ____. (Cuota de mercado).
When a company expands its operations by entering new, unrelated industries, it is called ____. (Diversificación).
questions.explanation: Diversification = diversificación (ej. entrar en sectores nuevos).

questions.question: When a company contracts out a business process to a third party, this is ____. (Subcontratación).
Relocating a business process from one country to another (usually to reduce costs) is called ____. (Deslocalización).
The main goal or purpose of a company, explaining why it exists, is its ____ statement. (Misión).
A company's aspirational description of what it wants to achieve in the future is its ____ statement. (Visión).
A newly introduced product or service that completely changes an industry is called a ____. (Disruptor).
To ensure long-term success, we must align our daily operations with our overall ____. (Estrategia).
questions.explanation: Strategy = estrategia general (vs tactics = acciones específicas).

questions.question: The difference between the value of a business and the value of its individual assets (often related to brand reputation) is called ____. (Fondo de comercio).
questions.explanation: Goodwill = fondo de comercio (valor intangible como la marca).

questions.question: The set of activities that a firm operating in a specific industry performs in order to deliver a valuable product is the value ____. (Cadena de valor).
When a company buys its suppliers to control the supply chain, it is called backward ____. (Integración hacia atrás).
A company that serves a very small, specialized segment of the market is operating in a ____ market. (Nicho).
The cost of passing up the next best choice when making a decision is the ____ cost. (Costo de oportunidad).
Core ____. (Competencia central con C)
Competitive ____. (Ventaja competitiva con A)
Blue ____ strategy. (Océano azul con O)
Economies of ____. (Escala con S)
A paradigm ____. (Cambio de paradigma con S)
A production ____. (Cuello de botella con B)
Market ____. (Cuota de mercado con S)
Product ____. (Diversificación con D)
IT ____. (Subcontratación con O)
A ____ market. (Mercado nicho con N)
